content: pytest defines 7 exit codes; exit 5 means 'No tests were collected'. A -k expression matching nothing yields exit 5, not 0 — so a shell && chain does fail, but the terminal output reads 'N deselected' with no failure line and is easily misread as green. There is no core --strict flag to turn no-collection into a failure; the docs point to the third-party pytest-custom_exit_code plugin. Practical audit rule: require a non-zero selected/passed count in the captured output, never rely on absence of failures.
